newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes rise, ANS business idle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes rise, ANS business idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose Wednesday with benchmark West Texas Intermediate (WTI), but bellweather Alaska North Slope (ANS) grade remained flat amid a lack of April business, players said.
Differentials for ANS remained $0.91 cents off WTI, but the grade's main seller withheld offers for April and May barrels. The seller took phone calls from refineries, but no bids were reported.
Texaco on Wedensday said it bought a full cargo of Colombian South Blend, an ANS lookalike which will load in late April for mid-May delivery.
The refinery said the cargo would displace its ANS requirements, and that another Northwest refiner was shopping for Colombian crudes.
A Los Angeles refinery considered Venezuelan crude, but declined to specify the grade, adding it was offered at $3.30 to 3.50 under WTI.
ARCO on Tuesday said it would ship 100 percent of April crude nominated on Line 63. No deals would get done until shippers had a few days to figure out their supply needs for the month.

One trader said demand for space could increase on Line 63 in May since Texaco and Unocal will return from shutdowns and Ultramar will resume buying High viscosity high sulfur crude after a month-long absense to use up inventories..
Outright prices for Kern River remained steady Tuesday. Kern River, a key heavy grade, ranged $15.00/15.10 a barrel.
